payload.title: Sand Ceremony Script With Sample Wording
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s, already planning a beach or destination ceremony with a 150k+ AUD budget, who want a sand ceremony that feels personal rather than generic and need ready-to-read wording their celebrant can use, plus the practical and legal questions answered before the day.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning a destination ceremony (single primary CTA, placed after the beach and destination practicalities section); one Wedded Advisor line in the close.
payload.angle: Most page-one scripts are one generic paragraph to copy. This guide gives original, ready-to-read wording in six tones (classic, short, romantic, family or blended family with children, beach and destination, non-religious), each split into celebrant introduction, the pour and the closing words, plus a fill-in template. It is honest about what a sand ceremony is not: it is symbolic and never replaces the legal words a celebrant and the couple must say in Australia, and abroad the destination country's law applies. It also turns the beach practicalities other pages skip (wind, permits, leaving no sand behind) into questions to ask the venue or council.
must_include: What a sand ceremony is and where it sits in the ceremony order, described as living practice only: no stated origins, history or fixed meanings
What you need: vessels (a keepsake vessel plus one per pourer), sand colours, a small table, and who pours (the couple, or family and children)

Several ORIGINAL sample scripts written by us, each with celebrant introduction, the pour and the closing words, in these tones: classic; short; romantic; family or blended family with children; beach and destination; non-religious
A fill-in template the reader can copy and give to their celebrant

Legal note: a sand ceremony is symbolic and does not replace the legal words a celebrant and the couple must say in Australia (Marriage Act 1961 ss45 and 46, wording reused from the short-wedding-vows source pack, official source at the claim); marrying abroad follows that country's law, link /expert-advice/should-you-marry-legally-abroad-or-have-a-symbolic-ceremony
Beach and destination practicalities framed as questions to the venue or local council: wind, permits, leaving no sand behind
Keeping the sand as a keepsake after the day
Close with one Wedded Advisor line drawn from content-system/brand/brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30, then the single primary CTA

Internal links: /expert-advice/what-happens-in-a-wedding-ceremony, /expert-advice/how-long-is-a-wedding-ceremony, /expert-advice/how-to-choose-a-wedding-celebrant, /expert-advice/what-does-a-celebrant-do-and-do-you-need-one-abroad, /expert-advice/should-you-marry-legally-abroad-or-have-a-symbolic-ceremony, /how-to-write-wedding-vows, /expert-advice/short-wedding-vows (draft), /expert-advice/wedding-processional-songs (draft), /expert-advice/vow-renewal-ideas, /style-advice/beach-wedding-dresses; planned WW-051 unity ceremony article as a placeholder LINK comment (no URL yet)

Stated origins, history or symbolic meanings presented as fact
Competitor wording or scripts (Easy Weddings or any other); all sample wording is original
Implying a sand ceremony has legal effect
